text:
jamie: @here heads-up: starting next Tuesday we will enable Just-In-Time (JIT) enforcement for privileged IAM roles in prod and staging. This blocks long-lived assume-role sessions and forces short-lived credentials for humans and automation. :warning:

jamie: Why: long-lived role sessions are a persistent attack vector. We saw a few service accounts using >24h sessions during the last audit. JIT reduces blast radius and makes rotations/forensics simpler.

jamie: What changes:
- Roles with no session-policy or with max-session-duration >1h will be denied at assume-role time.
- Service principals must use our credential broker (vault/oidc) or request explicit exceptions.
- People should shift interactive workflows to /access-request or the new SSO-permanent-session flow.

jamie: Required actions (owners):
1) By 2026-04-12 EOD: identify any automation, cron jobs, CI runners, or lambda-step functions that call assume-role with long durations.
2) Migrate those to short-lived tokens (STS, OIDC, or vault) or submit an exception at https://redwood.internal/security/exceptions with a remediation plan.
3) Update README/playbook references to the new flow.

jamie: Quick CLI checks you can run:
```bash
# list roles with long max session durations
aws iam list-roles --query 'Roles[?MaxSessionDuration>3600].[RoleName,MaxSessionDuration]' --output table

# find assumers in CloudTrail for long sessions (example)
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=AssumeRole --start-time 2026-03-01 --end-time 2026-04-01 --query 'Events[?contains(CloudTrailEvent, `AssumedRoleUser`) == `true`]' --output json | jq '.[] | {EventTime,Username: .Username,EventName}'
```

jamie: Playbook & rollout details: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/jit-priv-access (includes exception form, runbook, and contact points).

alex: What's the rollback plan if something critical breaks during enforcement?

jamie: Good Q — rollback is immediate disable of the enforcement flag via infra-ops. Deploy-bot will run a healthcheck and if >3 services fail auth, we auto-disable for 1 hour and open a PagerDuty incident to the infra-oncall rotation. We'll publish the rollback runbook in the playbook.

sasha: Are we expecting CI runners that need updates? I think a couple of our older workflows in tests/ci still assume long sessions.

jamie: Yes — CI is a likely hit. Owners: platform and eng-infra — we already flagged known pipelines and sent DMs. If you manage CI runners, please check the playbook page under "CI migration".

maria: If we need an exception for a vendor integration (can't use OIDC), what info do we need in the exception ticket?

jamie: Provide: the service owner, exact API calls, justification, remediation timeline (<=90 days), and compensating controls (IP allowlist, limited role scoping). We'll triage weekly.

deploy-bot: Policy rollout scheduled: 2026-04-13T02:00:00Z -> enforcement toggled on. Notification window: 72h prior.

infra-oncall: We'll be on standby during the window. If you expect planned deploys that assume long sessions, mark them in the exceptions form so SRE knows to monitor them.

alex: Can we get a short list of the top 10 roles likely affected? That would help teams prioritize.

jamie: Working on it — will post a CSV to the playbook by EOD today. If you want an ad-hoc scan for your account, DM me and I'll run it.

sasha: Thanks — will coordinate with platform. :thumbsup:

jamie: Thanks everyone. Summary: identify, migrate, or file exception by 2026-04-12. Reach out in-thread or ping me/eng-security for urgent questions.
